shared_elements: low-relief carving on a pale stone slab
sinuous snake-like or serpentine curved line
raised rounded ridges forming outlines rather than incised lines
horizontal arc or band spanning the upper part of the surface
motifs stacked vertically one above another
justification: Both surfaces show shallow, rounded-ridge relief on pale stone with motifs stacked vertically, and each carries a long sinuous serpentine line beneath an upper horizontal arc or band, which is the most specific correspondence. The biggest difference is content and legibility: B presents a crowded, clearly figurative programme of quadrupeds, birds and a human-like figure in ordered registers on a shaped pillar, whereas A shows only a few sparse, largely abstract or ambiguous forms on an irregular broken block.
